attempted_claim: Let X be a real Banach lattice with order-continuous norm and density character >= omega_1 (in particular, nonseparable). Does X necessarily contain an uncountable unconditional basic sequence in the long sense: a family (x_alpha)_{alpha<omega_1} of non-zero vectors and a constant K<infty such that for every finite F subset omega_1, scalars (a_alpha)_{alpha in F}, and signs (theta_alpha)_{alpha in F} with |theta_alpha|=1, ||sum_{alpha in F} theta_alpha a_alpha x_alpha|| <= K ||sum_{alpha in F} a_alpha x_alpha||? Asked in ZFC, as a finite-exact statement with uniform K, distinct from asymptotic ell_p(Gamma)/c_0(Gamma)-type classification and from axiom-conditional variants.
